thread:
ash (sec-eng): Heads up — triaging a cluster of Go deps flagged by vuln scanner this morning: grpc, oauth/jwt, and net/http-related packages. Initial severity looks medium → high for some call paths.

maria (backend): Can you paste the exact CVEs and which services depend on them?

ash (sec-eng): Sure. Summary from vuln-bot: 
- CVE-2026-0001: "grpc: header parsing edge-case leading to request spoofing" — affects google.golang.org/grpc versions < v1.55.3 (our product-api and router).
- CVE-2026-0012: "jwt library insufficient validation with certain alg combos" — affects github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.0.0 - v4.3.0 (auth-service).
- CVE-2026-0023: "net/http/httputil ReverseProxy can leak client headers on specific errors" — flagged in x/net/http2 and stdlib combos; upstream fix applied in go1.21.7 and backported in x/net v0.12.0 (edge-proxy).

sam (infra): vuln-bot posted bounty info too?

vuln-bot: [automated] findings: https://sec.example.com/reports/1790123456 — recommended pins: grpc@v1.55.3, golang-jwt@v4.4.1, golang.org/x/net@v0.12.0.

jordan (eng-sre): Ok. Impact: product-api (hosted) uses grpc heavily; auth-service uses golang-jwt; edge-proxy uses x/net/http2. Do we have pinned transitive deps or do we rely on indirect resolution?

ash (sec-eng): product-api currently pins google.golang.org/grpc in go.mod at v1.54.0 (direct). auth-service uses github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.3.0 (direct). edge-proxy doesn't pin x/net (indirect via http2 lib).

maria (backend): Proposed immediate actions: 
1) Patch product-api to grpc@v1.55.3 and run integration tests.
2) Patch auth-service to golang-jwt@v4.4.1 and add stricter alg enforcement in token parsing code.
3) Add a replace directive for golang.org/x/net@v0.12.0 in edge-proxy go.mod to force the fix, then run canary.

ash (sec-eng): I agree. Also recommend adding runtime checks for suspicious headers in ReverseProxy until we confirm canary results.

sam (infra): For rollout: canary on staging -> 5% traffic on prod cluster with circuit breaker -> full rollout. How long do we want the canary? 24h with alerting on error-rate and latency.

jordan (eng-sre): Set SLO watches: error rate > 0.5% or p50 latency +15% triggers rollback. I'll add dashboards and alerts.

maria (backend): Example go.mod changes for product-api:

```
module github.com/redwood/product-api

require (
    google.golang.org/grpc v1.55.3
    // other deps
)

// enforce transitive resolution for http2 if needed
replace golang.org/x/net => golang.org/x/net v0.12.0
```

ash (sec-eng): For auth-service, also tighten verification:

```go
// enforce alg and reject none
func parseToken(tokenStr string) (*jwt.Token, error) {
    token, err := jwt.Parse(tokenStr, keyFunc)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if token.Method.Alg() != expectedAlg {
        return nil, errors.New("unexpected signing algorithm")
    }
    return token, nil
}
```

maria (backend): Good. Also add unit tests for edge cases mentioned in CVE repro steps. I'll open PRs today.

sam (infra): One infra note: pinned replaces can hurt module caching on our build runners. I'll pre-warm module cache in CI and add a short-lived job to verify go mod download across services.

ash (sec-eng): Risk classification: grpc CVE: high for request forgery paths exposed to untrusted clients. jwt: medium-high if we accept mixed algs. net/http leak: medium but exploitable via specific proxy flows. Prioritize grpc and jwt for immediate patch; net/http can be canaried with replace.

jordan (eng-sre): Rollout plan summary (I'll own):
- Today: PRs opened for product-api and auth-service, edge-proxy replace PR.
- Tomorrow: CI green + staging canary 100% staging test run.
- +24h: 5% prod canary for product-api and edge-proxy with tight alerts.
- +48h: Gradual ramp if no regressions.

maria (backend): I'll tag the PRs with "sec: CVE-2026-0001/0012/0023" and include repro test cases.

ash (sec-eng): Add to audit log checklist: record KMS key usage if any token signing keys are rotated, and capture RBAC change notes if we touch service accounts. We need an entry in compliance ticketing for traceability.

sam (infra): We won't rotate KMS keys immediately — no key compromise. But if we push new token validation logic, we'll coordinate with identity team.

vuln-bot: [automated] New task created: SEC-4792 (go-deps-pinning) assigned to @maria and @ash.

ash (sec-eng): Thanks. Action items: @maria open PRs + tests; @sam prep CI cache job; @jordan create dashboards and run canary. I'll draft quick rollback procedures and update the incident runbook entry. Ping here when PRs are ready for review. :thumbsup:

maria (backend): PRs opened: product-api #412, auth-service #201, edge-proxy #88 — linking in the vuln ticket. Running unit tests now.

jordan (eng-sre): Dashboards up, canary runbook added to the ticket.

ash (sec-eng): Closing the triage for now — we'll monitor the canary and reconvene if any anomalies. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
